learn: A globe is a round model of Earth; maps are flat pictures of places.
Every flat map distorts something: shape, size or distance.
Map parts include a title, compass rose, scale and key (legend).
lessons.try: Compare Greenland's size on a flat map and on a globe.

learn: Lines of latitude run east-west and measure distance north or south of the equator.
Lines of longitude run north-south and measure distance east or west of the prime meridian.
Together they give absolute location, such as 40°N, 74°W for New York City.
lessons.try: Find the latitude and longitude of your town.

learn: Geographers use five themes: location, place, human-environment interaction, movement and region.
Place describes physical and human features. Region groups areas with something in common.
Movement studies how people, goods and ideas travel.
check: Groups of areas with something in common are...
How people change their environment is...
Trade between countries is an example of...
lessons.try: Describe your town using all five themes.

units.t: Early Humans and the Agricultural Revolution

learn: For most of human history, people were hunter-gatherers who moved to follow food.
Early humans made stone tools, used fire and created cave paintings like those at Lascaux in France.
Historians call this time the Stone Age (Paleolithic Era).
check: The Lascaux cave paintings are in...
The Old Stone Age is called the...
lessons.try: Draw a cave painting telling a story of a hunt.

learn: About 10,000 years ago, people began to farm and herd animals.
Farming meant people could settle in one place and store food.
The Fertile Crescent in Southwest Asia was one of the first farming regions.
check: One of the first farming regions was the...
lessons.try: List how life changed when people started farming.

learn: Food surpluses meant not everyone had to farm; people became potters, weavers and traders.
Villages grew into cities with governments, religions and social classes.
A civilization has cities, a government, specialised jobs, social classes, writing and art.
check: Which is a feature of civilization?
lessons.try: Make a chart of the features of a civilization.

learn: Mesopotamia means "land between the rivers": the Tigris and Euphrates, in modern-day Iraq.
Farmers dug canals to irrigate dry fields with river water.
Floods were unpredictable, so cooperation was needed.
lessons.try: Draw Mesopotamia with both rivers labelled.

learn: Sumerians built the first cities, such as Ur and Uruk, each an independent city-state.
Each city had a ziggurat, a stepped temple at its centre.
Sumerians invented cuneiform writing, the wheel and a number system based on 60.
lessons.try: Write your name in a cuneiform-style code using wedge marks in clay.

learn: Sargon of Akkad united the city-states into the first empire around 2300 BCE.
King Hammurabi of Babylon created one of the earliest written law codes, around 1750 BCE.
Hammurabi's Code applied laws publicly, though punishments depended on social class.
check: Who created an early written law code?
The first empire was founded by...
lessons.try: Discuss why written laws are fairer than unwritten ones.

learn: Egyptian civilization grew along the Nile River in northeast Africa.
Yearly floods left rich black soil for farming.
The river was also a highway for trade and travel.
lessons.try: Draw the Nile and label Upper and Lower Egypt.

learn: Pharaohs were kings believed to be gods on Earth.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BCE.
Egyptians mummified bodies because they believed in an afterlife.
check: The Great Pyramid was built for...
Mummification was linked to belief in...
lessons.try: Research one pharaoh and present three facts.

learn: Egyptians wrote in hieroglyphics on papyrus, a paper made from reeds.
The Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, helped scholars decode hieroglyphics.
Egyptians developed a 365-day calendar, medicine and geometry for building.
lessons.try: Write a message using a hieroglyph alphabet chart.

learn: One of the earliest civilizations grew along the Indus River in present-day Pakistan and India.
Cities like Mohenjo-daro had planned grid streets, brick houses and drainage systems.
Their writing has never been fully decoded.
check: The Indus Valley is in present-day...
lessons.try: Draw a plan of a grid city with drains.

learn: Hinduism developed over centuries and teaches dharma (duty) and karma (actions have consequences).
Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, around 500 BCE.
Buddhism teaches the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path to end suffering.
check: The Eightfold Path is part of...
lessons.try: Make a chart comparing the main ideas of Hinduism and Buddhism.

learn: The Maurya Empire united much of India. Emperor Ashoka turned to peace and Buddhism after a bloody war.
The Gupta Empire (about 320-550 CE) was a golden age of science and art.
Indian mathematicians developed the numerals 0-9 and the concept of zero we use today.
check: The Gupta era is called a...
lessons.try: Write the numbers 1 to 10 and note they came from India via Arab traders.

learn: Chinese civilization began along the Huang He (Yellow River).
Mountains and deserts isolated China, so it developed independently.
A dynasty is a series of rulers from one family; the Shang and Zhou were early dynasties.
check: A dynasty is a series of rulers from...
lessons.try: Draw a timeline of five Chinese dynasties.

learn: Confucius (551-479 BCE) taught respect for family, elders and good government.
The Mandate of Heaven said rulers had the gods' approval only if they ruled well.
Daoism taught living in harmony with nature.
check: The Mandate of Heaven depended on...
lessons.try: Discuss a saying of Confucius and what it means today.

learn: Shi Huangdi, the first Qin emperor, unified China and began the Great Wall.
He was buried with the Terracotta Army of thousands of clay soldiers.
The Han dynasty opened the Silk Road and invented paper. Later Chinese inventions include the compass and printing.
check: The first emperor of unified China was...
lessons.try: Make a list of Chinese inventions we still use.

learn: Greece's mountains and islands led to independent city-states called poleis.
Athens valued learning, art and democracy.
Sparta valued military strength; boys trained as soldiers from age seven.
lessons.try: Make a Venn diagram comparing Athens and Sparta.

learn: Democracy means "rule by the people".
In Athens, citizens voted directly on laws in an assembly.
Only free adult men were citizens; women, enslaved people and foreigners could not vote.
lessons.try: Hold a class vote and compare it to Athenian democracy.

learn: Greek philosophers Socrates, Plato and Aristotle asked big questions about truth and justice.
Greeks built temples like the Parthenon and wrote epic poems like Homer's "Odyssey".
The first Olympic Games were held in 776 BCE.
check: The first Olympic Games were in...
lessons.try: Read a short retelling of an episode from the "Odyssey".

learn: Rome was founded in Italy; legend says in 753 BCE.
In 509 BCE Romans set up a republic, where citizens elected leaders.
The Senate advised; two consuls led; a constitution set limits.
lessons.try: Compare the Roman Republic to the US government.

learn: Julius Caesar gained power and was killed in 44 BCE.
His heir Augustus became the first emperor; the Pax Romana, two centuries of peace, followed.
The empire stretched from Britain to Egypt.
lessons.try: Trace the Roman Empire on a map at its largest.

learn: Romans built roads, aqueducts and arches, and used concrete.
Latin became the root of Spanish, French, Italian and many English words.
Christianity began in the Roman Empire and became its official religion in 380 CE.
check: Christianity became Rome's official religion in...
lessons.try: Find five English words that come from Latin.

learn: The Maya lived in southern Mexico and Central America, building cities like Tikal and Chichén Itzá.
They built stepped pyramids, created a writing system and an accurate calendar.
Maya mathematicians used the concept of zero.
check: The Maya used the concept of...
lessons.try: Write numbers 1 to 10 in Maya dots and bars.

learn: The Aztecs built Tenochtitlan on an island in a lake, where Mexico City stands today.
They farmed on chinampas, floating gardens.
The Aztec Empire fell to Spanish conquerors and disease in 1521.
lessons.try: Draw a chinampa farm.

learn: The Inca Empire stretched along the Andes Mountains in South America.
They built Machu Picchu, terraced farms and thousands of miles of roads.
The Inca kept records using quipu, knotted strings.
check: Machu Picchu was built by the...
lessons.try: Make a quipu with string to record a number.

learn: Geographers divide the world into regions such as North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa, Southwest Asia, South Asia, East Asia and Oceania.
Regions share features like landforms, climate, language or culture.
Ancient civilizations shaped many of today's countries.
lessons.try: Colour a world map by region.

learn: Culture includes language, religion, food, clothing, art and customs.
Cultures spread through trade, migration and technology.
Respecting other cultures helps people live and work together.
lessons.try: Interview someone about their family's traditions.

learn: Many modern ideas come from ancient civilizations: democracy, law codes, numerals and paper.
Historians use primary sources (made at the time) and secondary sources (written later).
Studying the past helps us understand the present.
lessons.try: List three things in your day that came from an ancient civilization.
